help.title: Help
help.protection: When a FoxHole Core profile starts or its connection fails unexpectedly, traffic directed to VPN is blocked even if “Block on VPN loss” is disabled. After Stop, blocking remains if that setting is enabled. Explicit “Without VPN” device rules still apply when local network rules are enabled; website and country exceptions do not apply during emergency blocking.
help.connect_save: Paste your Hysteria 2 configuration and save.
help.connect_start: Open the server and press Connect.
help.test_note: Test validates the configuration format, not connectivity.
help.rules_direct: New rules use direct access. Select VPN when a tunnel is required.
help.rules_order: With local network rules enabled, the first matching device rule in saved order applies. “Without VPN” for a device takes priority over websites and countries. For a device set to “Through VPN”, website rules are then considered: “Through VPN” first, then “Without VPN”, followed by country exceptions. The remaining traffic from that device uses VPN.
help.rules_dns: Use router DNS for domain rules. Encrypted DNS and shared website IPs limit matching.
help.rules_country: Country is determined by IP allocation, not website ownership.
help.vpn_measurement: A public HTTPS request through the tunnel. Missing measurements stay unavailable.
help.access_pin: Change PIN only through LuCI. The panel PIN is separate from the router password.
help.access_recovery: Forgot your PIN? Sign in to LuCI and open Change PIN.
help.access_clients: The incoming home VPN server is off by default. Turn on “Home VPN server” in Settings and confirm the verified Hysteria2 component. Turning it off stops the server and hides VPN clients; profiles, keys and pairings are preserved. A static public IPv4 address and an externally reachable UDP port are required. Creating a profile does not prove port availability. LAN access is granted separately. The component is kept when turned off unless its removal is selected in the confirmation dialog.
help.access_client_port: To connect to a remote server, use the port from its configuration: it is not necessarily 443. Importing a profile does not change the VPS port. Incoming router clients share UDP/443; in separate-port mode, use the port from the issued link.
help.hiddify: Hiddify: import the hysteria2:// link from the clipboard. Connection refused on 127.0.0.1 while adding a profile indicates an unavailable local app component, not the router port. Fully restart Hiddify and retry; if it repeats, check the app version and logs.

about.title: About
about.description: FoxHole OpenWrt manages VPN connections and installed FoxHole Core modules on an OpenWrt router.
logs.flash_policy: On FLASH, observations are retained for up to 30 days. New entries replace the oldest in a bounded buffer. Entry time is when the event was first observed.
manual.intro: Features depend on installed modules and the current build.
manual.start.title: Get started
manual.start.one: Open LuCI → Services → FoxHole from your local network.
manual.start.two: On first use, read the agreement and choose your own panel PIN. It is not your OpenWrt password.
manual.start.three: Add a compatible VPN profile, open it and select Connect.
manual.start.four: Wait for connection status, then test a site from a device on your network.
manual.start.note: You need your own VPN server or a provider subscription. Test checks configuration format separately from network reachability: a TCP port connection or, for UDP, host reachability. It does not confirm a VPN handshake or credentials.
manual.start.install: Install the FoxHole package separately using the official instructions for a supported firmware and target. FoxHole does not install OpenWrt firmware.
manual.profiles.title: VPN profiles and modules
manual.profiles.body: A profile stores your VPN server settings. Connecting requires a compatible installed module. Availability depends on firmware, architecture and the verified catalog. Add missing protocols separately in the protocol section.
manual.profiles.editor: Manual addition in this editor is for Hysteria 2. Use a supported link or configuration. Transfer other profiles through an available path in the paired app.
manual.profiles.legacy: Updating the panel does not install missing protocols automatically. The legacy Hysteria engine is not automatically migrated into Core.
manual.routing.title: Routing rules
manual.routing.body: Enable local-network rules and choose their scope. Select VPN or Direct for a device or address.
manual.routing.devices: A Direct device rule takes priority over site and country rules. Device rules use the first match in saved order.
manual.routing.vpn: Other traffic in the rule scope first uses VPN site rules.
manual.routing.countries: Country exceptions follow. Remaining traffic is sent through VPN.
manual.routing.note: Local and reserved addresses are handled separately. Country rules use IP ranges, not the website owner or the exact location of its content.
manual.dns.title: Domains and DNS
manual.dns.body: Domain rules use the router’s DNS answers. Enter a domain such as example.com or a leading pattern such as *.example.com. Page paths and URL parameters are not separate rules.
manual.dns.limits: A device’s own encrypted DNS and shared website IPs limit accuracy. Arbitrary * patterns and ? masks are not supported yet. A compatible dnsmasq with nftset is required.
manual.blocking.title: Blocking
manual.blocking.start: When a VPN connection starts or drops, traffic routed through that VPN tunnel is blocked regardless of the separate block toggle.
manual.blocking.stop: After an explicit Stop, blocking remains if that switch is enabled.
manual.blocking.direct: Explicit Direct device rules remain exceptions when local-network rules are enabled.
manual.blocking.notice: Site and country exceptions do not apply during emergency blocking. This is not an unconditional block on the whole router. Incoming Hysteria clients have separate routes, ACLs and direct-fallback conditions.
manual.phone.title: Phone and VPN profile transfer
manual.phone.body: For first pairing, connect your phone to the router’s Wi-Fi network and open Router in FoxHole Guard or FoxHole VPN. Confirm its verified identity and enter the panel PIN. Transfer saves the selected configuration; start VPN on the router separately.
manual.phone.vpn: Open the desired profile’s actions → Send Configuration to Router. For a subscription, choose a server and protocol first. You can also use + at the top of Management to select several compatible saved profiles and tap Save. Then select a transferred profile under Router → Management and start it separately.
manual.phone.guard: During pairing, select the desired VPN Profile and complete the wizard. To add profiles later, open Management and tap + at the top. Select one or more compatible saved profiles and tap Save. The list reflects the router’s supported protocols and installed modules. Then select a transferred profile under Management and start it separately.
manual.phone.pin: Changing the PIN through an authorized flow resets pairings but keeps VPN profiles and settings. Revoking a pairing disables phone management; an incoming VPN client must be removed separately. To send saved profiles from a phone, open Router management and tap Add VPN profile.
manual.phone.trust: Pairing does not create an incoming VPN automatically or enable continuous two-way synchronization. Automatic installation from Android apps is available only after pairing.
manual.clients.title: Incoming VPN clients
manual.clients.body: VPN profiles define outbound connections. VPN clients connect to this router’s inbound server. A separate Hysteria2 server component is installed for this; a public WAN address and an externally reachable UDP port are required. Client access to the LAN is configured separately.
manual.clients.privacy: QR codes and links contain access credentials. Share them only with the intended device owner. Re-exporting a configuration or QR does not rotate keys.
manual.clients.revoke: Remove the relevant client to revoke its incoming VPN access.
manual.clients.home: Management through the trusted home VPN is enabled separately for an existing pairing and does not open a management port on the WAN.
manual.updates.title: Updates
manual.updates.body: Open Settings → Application update, check the available version and review changes. Updates cover FoxHole and selected installed modules, not OpenWrt firmware or unrelated packages. An active component update may reconnect VPN. Do not power off the router during installation.
manual.updates.auto: Automatic updating checks at most once per day. You can opt out during fresh web or Android setup; an existing choice is preserved. CLI installation leaves it off by default.
manual.updates.lost: If a response is lost, sign in again and read status. Do not blindly repeat Apply. Check failed does not mean up to date. Recovery required needs separate attention.
manual.updates.core: Core and the panel package are checked separately: Core-current does not prove package-current. Phone relay is allowed only through the verified protocol after a proven network problem. Explicitly stop active legacy Hysteria if the updater requests it.
manual.storage.title: Storage
manual.storage.flash: Install to the router’s internal storage.
manual.storage.settings: Settings are stored separately. Available modes depend on the verified catalog and resources. Log availability depends on where FoxHole is installed.
manual.storage.bootstrap: A standalone engine in RAM and a full native RAM package are different modes.
manual.privacy.title: Backup and privacy
manual.privacy.backup: If available, review the backup contents before saving or restoring it.
manual.privacy.restore: Ordinary restore does not import the panel PIN, pairings or current router identity. The connection may reconnect.
manual.privacy.online: History and state are stored locally. Updates use GitHub and external country feeds; IP probes may contact Cloudflare. Never publish profiles, subscriptions, QR codes or backups.
manual.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics and troubleshooting
manual.diagnostics.body: The journal contains selected diagnostic events and the last available Core state. It is not a full traffic log or every past error. Use HTTPS for the standalone panel; refresh the displayed list manually.
manual.problem.pin.title: PIN rejected
manual.problem.pin.body: Use the FoxHole panel PIN, not your OpenWrt password. Wait for a displayed cooldown. Use the authorized LuCI recovery path when needed.
manual.problem.test.title: Test passes but VPN does not connect
manual.problem.test.body: Format validation and network reachability are reported separately. An accessible TCP port or responsive UDP host does not prove VPN protocol operation or authentication. Check the server, port and connection status. Keep certificate verification enabled.
manual.problem.dns.title: Domain rules do not apply
manual.problem.dns.body: Check rule scope and the device’s DNS. Encrypted DNS and shared IPs can limit classification.
manual.problem.module.title: Protocol unavailable
manual.problem.module.body: Use a verified published module for the exact firmware and target. A similarly named ARM build is not proof of compatibility.
manual.problem.memory.title: Not enough memory
manual.problem.memory.body: Read the current installation or recovery status. Do not remove arbitrary system files or bypass reserved-resource checks.
manual.problem.lost.title: Update or restore response lost
manual.problem.lost.body: Reconnect to the panel and read status before applying the operation again.
manual.problem.remote.title: Remote client cannot connect
manual.problem.remote.body: Check the separate server package and outside UDP reachability. A public IP alone does not prove port reachability. Do not expose the management port to the Internet.
manual.problem.stale.title: Data or source unavailable
manual.problem.stale.body: Check the last observation time and refresh. Missing data does not mean no errors occurred.
manual.current.title: Current version and limitations
manual.current.body: These are available facts about the installed package and modules. Module versions may differ from the panel version. Open the update section in Settings to check for updates. Added support for OpenWrt 25.12.6.
manual.current.requirements: This build targets OpenWrt 25.12.5 or 25.12.6 with apk and verified targets. Code or module presence does not establish hardware qualification. Unavailable, not released and unsupported are different states.
server.test_tcp: Configuration format is valid. The server TCP port is reachable; VPN authentication was not tested.
server.test_host: Configuration format is valid. The host responds; the UDP service and VPN authentication were not tested.
server.test_unconfirmed: Configuration is valid, but server reachability could not be confirmed. ICMP may be blocked.
server.test_blocked: Configuration is valid. Network testing of private or local addresses is disabled.
manual.diagnostics.measurements: When measurements are missing, the chart line drops to the baseline and resumes when data returns. This marks a gap, not a measured zero. About reads the installation method and verified installed Core modules independently of update availability; a separate legacy Hysteria client is not a Core module.
